subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: The Garden City Movement
description: One-minute skill: The Garden City Movement.

hook.text: In 1898, Ebenezer Howard proposed a radical idea: cities surrounded by permanent green belts no one could build on.

buildup.text: His Garden Cities combined town and country — walkable neighborhoods ringed by farms and forests.

discovery.text: Letchworth and Welwyn were built as prototypes. Wide streets, gardens, and communal green space defined them.

twist.text: Developers copied the aesthetics — curving streets, cul-de-sacs — but ignored the communal land ownership.

climax.text: The suburb borrowed Howard's look and abandoned his values. Sprawl is the Garden City's evil twin.

punchline.text: He imagined green utopias. We built strip malls instead.

quiz.question: What key feature of the Garden City did suburban developers ignore?
options: The use of curving streets and cul-de-sacs
Communal land ownership and permanent green belts
The requirement for single-family detached houses
